misconceptions.description: Submitting one document and treating it as the complete brand package the studio requires
misconceptions.trigger: learner turns in only a resume or only a LinkedIn screenshot
misconceptions.feedback: The package integrates resume, bio, LinkedIn, portfolio, and an AI-use log. One isolated file is not the package.

misconceptions.description: Spending the final pass matching fonts and colors while leaving contradictory facts across artifacts
misconceptions.trigger: learner fixes visual style but misses conflicting dates, titles, or accomplishments
misconceptions.feedback: Fix factual contradictions first. Two different graduation dates break trust; matching fonts does not earn it.

misconceptions.description: Letting AI produce the entire brand package and submitting it without exercising or recording judgment
misconceptions.trigger: learner's AI-use log shows the tool did the work and the student only submitted it
misconceptions.feedback: Use AI for bounded help, then choose, reject, and rewrite. The log should show your judgment on top of the tool's output.

misconceptions.description: Judging the package ready because it looks polished, rather than because it is consistent and accountable
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits based on visual polish without a cross-artifact consistency check or AI-use log
misconceptions.feedback: Readiness is consistency plus accountability. Confirm the facts agree across artifacts and the AI-use log is complete.
